hero.heading: Steal Animal Egg Wiki
hero.lead: Steal Animal Egg by Sillytung Studios is a Roblox game about taking eggs from animals, hatching pets, earning from pets, eating food, and stealing from other players.
hero.supportingText: This wiki covers the Sillytung Studios experience, place ID 99679692310083. Start with the codes or first-session guide, then compare the pets you hatch.

sections.heading: What Is Steal Animal Egg?
paragraphs: Steal Animal Egg combines egg collecting with a growing pet collection. The basic idea is easy to follow: take an egg, hatch it, and earn from the pet you receive. Food and stealing from other players are also part of the game. Different egg sizes and mutations give you more details to pay attention to as you learn the loop.

This Steal Animal Egg wiki is an independent guide for the Roblox experience made by Sillytung Studios. Use the Play on Roblox button above to reach that game directly. Similar titles can appear in search results, so check the creator before following a code list or a gameplay guide. Matching the game matters more than matching a familiar-looking title.

You do not need to memorize every animal or chase the most impressive-looking egg before starting. A useful first goal is to complete the egg-to-pet loop and understand the information the game shows you. Once you can repeat that comfortably, you can make better choices about which targets to try and which earnings to compare.

sections.heading: How Steal Animal Egg Gameplay Works

subsections.heading: Take eggs from animals
paragraphs: Taking eggs from animals is the starting point of the official game loop. Look at the interaction prompt shown in your own session rather than assuming a button from another device. Choose an egg you can reach and plan what you will do after taking it. A clear return plan is more useful than committing to an unfamiliar target just because it looks appealing.

subsections.heading: Hatch eggs to collect pets
paragraphs: Hatching turns egg collection into pet collection. Follow the instructions at the appropriate area in your session and complete the process before heading out again. Read the resulting pet name and any displayed details. There is no need to assume a fixed hatch duration, guaranteed animal, or universal set of odds when the live game can show you the next action.

subsections.heading: Earn from pets
paragraphs: Pets provide earnings. The practical comparison is the number shown for your own pet and the basis on which it is measured. Check whether a display refers to one pet or your total collection before comparing it with another screen. A number copied without its label can lead to a poor choice even when the number itself is correct.

subsections.heading: Eat food
paragraphs: Eating food is part of Steal Animal Egg. Read the item description and the current interaction prompt before using food, then check what changes in your session. Use each food’s own description to understand its effect. If you are deciding how to spend earnings, use the displayed information and keep your immediate progression goal in mind.

subsections.heading: Steal from other players
paragraphs: The game also includes stealing from other players. Treat this as a separate situation from taking eggs from animals: another player can change what happens while you are planning. Learn your usual return route first, watch the current situation, and use the stealing guide when you want a more deliberate approach to an attempt.

subsections.heading: Discover egg sizes and mutations
paragraphs: The official description highlights egg sizes and mutations. Notice those details while collecting and compare the resulting pet information after hatching. Keep size and variant labels alongside the displayed earnings so you can match the entry to the pet in your collection.

sections.heading: Steal Animal Egg Guides and References
paragraphs: The beginner progression guide gives you a manageable order of tasks. It helps when you have just joined and do not yet know which screen or action deserves your attention. The stealing guide takes a narrower view: choose a reachable target, know the way back, follow the live prompt, and finish the attempt before assessing the result.

The three collection references answer different questions. All Animals explains what you are looking at. The Tier List helps decide what to prioritize. The Value List explains how to compare displayed earnings. Start with identification when a pet is unfamiliar, then move to comparison when you have two or more options in front of you.

sections.heading: Animals, Income, Sizes and Mutations
paragraphs: Animal names, income, sizes, and mutations are central to understanding a collection. Keep the name separate from the other details: two pets that look similar may still show different information. Record the exact label you see rather than shortening it into a category that might mix several entries together.

For progression decisions, compare earnings under similar conditions and read the units. Use rarity and appearance as additional context when the game displays them. They should not replace the earning figure or create a guaranteed multiplier. Your own collection is the most relevant starting point because it reflects the pets and variants available to you right now.

sections.heading: How to Steal Eggs
paragraphs: Before taking an egg, identify the route back to the area where you can complete the hatch loop. Choose a manageable target and use the prompt shown by the game. Taking the egg is one part of the attempt; getting it back and completing the next action is what connects the attempt to your collection.

Taking eggs from animals and stealing from players are both described by the creator, but they are not interchangeable instructions. For player stealing, inspect the live situation rather than assuming fixed locks, timers, or defenses. If an attempt goes badly, identify the part that failed and adjust one decision on the next run.
